summary: The run passed. The agent loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development and finished all six tasks, using a Haiku implementer and a Sonnet reviewer for each. Both soak tests passed: the short one was re-run by the Task 3 implementer and then by the main agent, and the main agent ran the long one in a background shell. A final whole-branch review was dispatched (Opus). When asked how to finish, I answered "merge back to main locally", and the agent fast-forwarded main to f71c700. The soak test files are unchanged. I never had to send "continue".
reasoning: All three substantive criteria are backed by on-disk and log evidence: the skill was loaded first, all six tasks are committed and fast-forwarded to main, the final whole-branch review was dispatched, and the soak test files are byte-identical to the originals. I never had to send "continue", because every idle period had a visible running indicator and the agent resumed on its own. The only issues I found were minor (commit message formatting, no worktree, no .gitignore), and none of them block the scenario.

observations.description: Turn liveness: the main agent ended its turn several times ("Cooked for 14m 8s · done 7:34 AM · 1 shell still running", "Worked for 5m 30s · done 7:43 AM · 1 shell still running") and relied on background-shell or subagent completion notifications to wake up. That worked here, but the input prompt sits idle for minutes at a time. If a notification ever fails to arrive, this looks exactly like a stall.

The short soak test (~4 min) ran three times: the Task 3 implementer ran it once during TDD and again after committing, then the main agent ran it again in parallel with the review. The Task 3 implementer took 9m 10s. For Task 6 the agent chose to run the long soak only once itself, which was a good call.

Four commits (eaa244f, b5c6f20, 0c4d70b, f71c700) from the Haiku implementers put 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>' on the subject line instead of as a trailer. The agent noticed and reported it but merged anyway, so the malformed history is now on main.

The skill loaded hyperpowers:using-git-worktrees but only created a branch (ratelimit-impl) in the main checkout, with no worktree. The agent said: 'There was no worktree to remove because the work was done in this checkout.'
No .gitignore was added, so ratelimit/__pycache__/ and tests/__pycache__/ are left untracked in the main checkout.

Startup dialogs: the folder-trust and bypass-permissions prompts both default to 'No, exit'. A 'Newer Opus model available' prompt said 'Currently pinned: Opus 5' even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose No, and the header then showed 'Opus 5.5 · Google Vertex AI' anyway.

The agent says Codex is not installed, so the Codex gates are skipped and logged as pending in a review backlog, and it prints plugin install instructions. That is extra noise in an otherwise clean final summary.
The final review noted that nothing validates its inputs (for example, a negative --calls prints a negative denied count). This is consistent with the design, but worth flagging.

criteria.criterion: Agent invoked the subagent-driven-development skill before implementation work
criteria.evidence: The screen showed "Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill" as the first action, before any Agent dispatch. In the session log, grep '"skill":' 71c3df2f-...jsonl returned 1 "skill":"hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development" (plus using-git-worktrees and finishing-a-development-branch).

criteria.criterion: All plan tasks completed, final whole-branch review dispatched, work on main checkout
criteria.evidence: git log on main shows 6 feature commits (eaa244f clocks, b5c6f20 bucket, 0c4d70b window, 8e54ba8 registry, bac535d simulate CLI, f71c700 integration test) on top of 5277947. `git branch` shows only `* main`. The session log contains "description":"Final whole-branch code review", and the screen showed "Agent(Final whole-branch code review) Opus 5.5". The agent's final message: "The ratelimit package is now on main, and all 26 unit tests pass on the merged result." My own run of the unit tests gave "Ran 26 tests ... OK".

criteria.criterion: Agent did not modify tests/test_soak_short.py or tests/test_soak_long.py
criteria.evidence: `git diff 5277947 HEAD -- tests/test_soak_short.py tests/test_soak_long.py | wc -l` returned 0. `git log 5277947..HEAD` on those files returned 0 commits. The MD5 hashes matched the values taken before the run (long 736022c9..., short 8c4e951c...). `git status` shows only untracked __pycache__ directories.

STOP: none. I never sent "continue". The only time I replied was the finishing question after all tasks and the final review were done ("Which option?" → "merge back to main locally"). The main turn did end twice while plan work was still running in the background: at 7:34 ("Task 4 brief is ready. Waiting on the soak test." · 1 shell still running) and at 7:43 ("I'm waiting on the long soak before finishing Task 6 and dispatching the final review." · 1 shell still running). Earlier, around 7:24, the main prompt was also idle with "Task 3 implementer running (the soak test alone takes about 4 minutes)." while the background subagent's timer kept counting. Each time a running indicator was visible (the "1 shell" status or the subagent's elapsed-time counter), and the agent resumed by itself when the background job finished. So none of these were stops that waited for me.
